definitions.gloss: mixing public and private matters; confusing official and personal business
definitions.explanation: Failing to maintain proper boundaries between one's public/professional role and private affairs. Generally used critically to describe improper behavior.

examples.japanese: {公私混同|こうしこんどう}はよくない。
examples.english: Mixing public and private matters is not good.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{経費|けいひ}で{私用|しよう}の{買|か}い{物|もの}をするのは{公私混同|こうしこんどう}だ。
examples.english: Using company expenses for personal shopping is mixing public and private matters.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}が{部下|ぶか}に{私的|してき}な{用事|ようじ}を{頼|たの}むのは{公私混同|こうしこんどう}と{言|い}われても{仕方|しかた}ない。
examples.english: When a boss asks a subordinate to handle personal errands, it can't help but be called a mixing of public and private.

notes:
A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) composed of {公|こう} (public), {私|し} (private), {混|こん} (mix), and {同|どう} (same/together). Almost always used with a negative connotation to criticize someone who blurs the line between their official duties and personal interests.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {公私混同|こうしこんどう}する — to mix public and private matters
- {公私混同|こうしこんどう}を{避|さ}ける — to avoid mixing public and private
- {公私|こうし}の{区別|くべつ} — distinction between public and private

USAGE:
Commonly brought up in workplace ethics discussions. The phrase carries inherent criticism — it implies the person is abusing their position or being unprofessional. Related to the ideal of {公私|こうし}の{区別|くべつ}をつける (maintaining the distinction between public and private).
